hints.content: Draw or imagine unit fractions with a small, concrete example before using symbols.
Test your idea against a simple counter-example: change one quantity and check whether the relationship still holds.
Write the known quantities first, then apply the operation that keeps the equation or relationship balanced.
Think of unit fractions as a relationship that stays consistent even when the representation changes.
Point to the first step where your written work changes the quantity or structure unexpectedly.
Use one whole, split into equal parts, and name the part that the numerator counts.
Circle the operation closest to the unknown. Undo that operation first and record the same change on both sides.
Ask whether your rule works for a boundary case such as zero, one, or an equal pair of quantities.
Translate the symbols into a sentence, solve the sentence, and translate the result back.
Check units, signs, and the order of quantities before checking arithmetic.
